source.publication: 2025 NJ-1040 Instructions (with GIT-1 & 2 Retirement Income, January 2026, and njit6/njit7 web pages where named)
source.section: Form NJ-1040 lines 6, 7, 13, 30: Instr PDF p.8 Line 6 Regular Exemptions and Line 7 Senior 65+ ('born in 1960 or earlier'), PDF p.9 line 13; lines 15, 27, 29, 38-43: PDF p.8 lines 6-7 (regular and senior 65+ exemptions), PDF p.9 line 13, PDF p.25 line 30, PDF p.27 lines 38-39, PDF p.33 lines 42-43, PDF p.65 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Federal AGI 100,000.00 (wages 70,000.00 + 30,000.00); federal taxable income = 100,000.00 - 33,100.00 federal standard deduction (31,500 joint + 1,600 for the one spouse 65 or older) = 66,900.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Line 15 wages 70,000.00 + 30,000.00 = line 27 total income 100,000.00. Lines 28a-28b: no pension, annuity or IRA income and wages over 3,000, so no exclusion; exclusions 0.00. Spouse 1 was born 1960-12-31 and is 65 on the last day of the year, so he takes the senior exemption; spouse 2 (58) does not. Line 29 New Jersey gross income = 100,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 100,000.00. Line 30 exemptions (line 13): regular 1,000 x 2 + senior 65+ 1,000 x 1 = 3,000.00; line 38 = 3,000.00 (no other deductions). Line 39/42 taxable income = 100,000.00 - 3,000.00 = 97,000.00. Line 43 tax, rate schedule Table B (joint/head of household/qualifying widow(er)) as bands: 20,000.00 x 0.014 = 280.00 + 30,000.00 x 0.0175 = 525.00 + 20,000.00 x 0.0245 = 490.00 + 10,000.00 x 0.035 = 350.00 + 17,000.00 x 0.05525 = 939.25 = 2,584.25. The booklet's Tax Table (taxable income under 100,000) gives 2,586 for the 97,000-97,050 row (schedule at the midpoint 97,025, rounded); expected keeps the exact schedule result. No credits. State income tax = 2,584.25.
accepted_approximations: Tax Table: for taxable income under 100,000 New Jersey uses its Tax Table, the schedule's tax at each 50-dollar row's midpoint rounded to the dollar; the projection uses the exact schedule.
